Home.title: Having a beautiful smile increases your self‑esteem and the confidence with which you move through the world.

image.alt: Happy people showing beautiful smiles at Tyska Alexander Orthodontics

paragraphs.text: Having a beautiful smile increases your self‑esteem and the confidence with which you move through the world. Dr. Edwin Tyska and Dr. Kristen Alexander excel at creating incredible smiles that are healthy and becoming. Our doctors achieve excellent clinical results because they consult together when they design a treatment plan for each patient.

Each treatment plan is unique to you and your needs: our doctors pay attention to details that less-experienced providers might overlook to make your mouth healthy and your smile beautiful. Our experienced orthodontic team supports you through every step, and we offer complimentary consultations at our Clarence and Tonawanda offices.

items.title: Collaborative Team
items.text: Every treatment plan is reviewed by our doctors together so you benefit from multiple experienced orthodontists.

items.title: Personalized Care
items.text: We design customized treatment plans that focus on both oral health and the cosmetic results you want.

items.title: Modern Technology
items.text: We offer clear and metal braces, Invisalign<sup>®</sup>/Invisalign Teen®, iTero digital impressions and Orthopulse® options for precise, comfortable care.

items.title: Friendly Team
items.text: Our compassionate, experienced team supports patients from a complimentary consultation through retention, making every visit easy.

In-house financing with low monthly payments is available, and we offer complimentary, no‑obligation consultations at both our Tonawanda and Clarence offices. For billing or insurance questions call Clarence at (716) 759‑8323 or Tonawanda at (716) 875‑0405.

Please print and complete your patient information before your first appointment, or complete forms securely online using our patient portal. Finishing forms ahead of time speeds check-in and helps us provide safe, personalized care.

Treatments.title: Treatments — Options for every age and smile

image.alt: Smiling patients of all ages at Lakeshore Orthodontics

Treatments.title: Early (Phase One) orthodontic treatment — when to start and why

paragraphs.text: Early treatment, often called Phase One, typically begins around age eight or nine; Phase Two usually starts around age 11 or older. The goal is to guide jaw growth, correct bite problems such as underbites or crossbites, and make room for permanent teeth so extractions are less likely later.

accordion.header: When to start

paragraphs.text: Look for early or late loss of baby teeth, difficulty chewing, persistent thumb-sucking after age five, mouth breathing, or crowded front teeth by age seven or eight. These signs can mean it’s time for an evaluation.

image.alt: Young patient receiving early orthodontic intervention

accordion.header: Signs your child may need treatment

paragraphs.text: Speech issues, protruding teeth, crossbites, or crowding in the front teeth are common reasons families seek an early consult. Addressing these early can simplify later care.

image.alt: Teen patient smiling with braces

accordion.header: Benefits of early care

paragraphs.text: Early intervention can direct jaw growth, reduce the severity of future problems, decrease the likelihood of extractions or surgery, and often shorten later treatment time.

image.alt: Adult patient receiving orthodontic treatment
Smiling family enjoying time together

Treatments.title: Orthodontics for adults — it's never too late

paragraphs.text: Many adults choose orthodontics to correct a bite, address crowding or spacing, restore a worn smile, or finish treatment started years ago. Because jaw growth is complete, adult plans consider gum and bone health and coordinate with restorative dentistry when needed.

accordion.header: Discreet options for adults

paragraphs.text: Clear aligners such as Invisalign<sup>®</sup>, ceramic (clear) braces, and low-visibility bracket systems give adults effective, less noticeable ways to straighten teeth.

image.alt: Smiling Woman with Clear Aligner

accordion.header: What to expect

paragraphs.text: Treatment is personalized, may involve coordination with periodontists or general dentists, and focuses on creating a healthy, stable bite that is easier to keep clean.

image.alt: Two stylish smiling teens taking selfie with braces
Adult patient receiving orthodontic treatment

accordion.header: Traditional Metal Braces

paragraphs.text: Metal braces use small brackets and archwires to move teeth predictably. They are durable, cost-effective, and now more comfortable and discreet than in the past.

image.alt: Dental Checkup with Braces

accordion.header: Ceramic (clear) braces

paragraphs.text: Ceramic braces blend with your tooth color to be less noticeable while delivering effective tooth movement. Good oral hygiene is important to keep them looking their best.

image.alt: Smiling Woman with Clear Aligner
Two stylish smiling teens taking selfie with braces

Treatments.title: Invisalign<sup>®</sup> clear aligners — how they work and candidates

paragraphs.text: Invisalign<sup>®</sup> uses a series of clear, removable aligners to move teeth gently. Aligners are custom-made from digital scans and are removable for eating and oral hygiene, which many patients find convenient.

Typical process: consultation, digital scan (iTero) and 3D treatment plan, a series of aligners worn about 20 to 22 hours per day, periodic progress checks, and a retainer such as Vivera at completion. Suitability is determined during consultation based on the complexity of movements and oral health.

image.alt: Close-up of Invisalign aligners being placed on teeth

paragraphs.text: Orthognathic surgery is recommended when jaw misalignment cannot be corrected with orthodontics alone. Surgery is typically considered after growth is complete, with presurgical orthodontics to align the teeth followed by hospital-based corrective surgery.

The process includes collaborative planning between the orthodontist and an oral and maxillofacial surgeon, a recovery period of about two weeks, and follow-up orthodontics to fine-tune the bite. Risks and benefits will be discussed in detail during consultation.

image.alt: Orthodontic patient receiving orthognathic surgical consultation

paragraphs.text: Maintain your new smile with custom retainers made for comfort and stability. We offer removable wire-and-acrylic retainers, clear aligner-style Essix retainers, and fixed bonded retainers placed behind the teeth.

Wear schedules are personalized; many patients wear a retainer full-time for a short period, then nightly long term to prevent regression. Good oral hygiene and regular checkups help keep results stable.

image.alt: Beautiful young Asian woman smiling and holding orthodontic retainer

paragraphs.text: We use digital tools to improve precision and comfort. Fast, radiation-free 3D scanning, digital X-rays, and 3D treatment planning help us design predictable, efficient care and let patients preview likely results.

accordion.header: iTero digital scanning

paragraphs.text: iTero scanners capture fast, accurate 3D impressions without messy putty. These scans are used for aligner workflows and to create detailed treatment plans.

image.alt: iTero digital scanner in use during orthodontic consultation

accordion.header: Digital X-rays

paragraphs.text: High-resolution digital radiography provides detailed imagery with less radiation than older film methods, speeding diagnosis and treatment planning.

image.alt: Digital X-ray equipment showing detailed orthodontic imaging

accordion.header: 3D treatment planning

paragraphs.text: Advanced software simulates each stage of tooth movement so we can refine the plan and show a virtual preview of expected changes.

image.alt: 3D treatment planning software showing orthodontic simulation

FAQ.title: Frequently Asked Questions — Answers for our patients

image.alt: Patient consultation and treatment in a modern orthodontic office

paragraphs.text: Have a question about treatment options, insurance, appointments, or how to care for your braces or aligners? Below are the most common patient questions and quick, practical answers to help you prepare for your visit and make the most of your treatment.

accordion.header: What treatment options do you offer?

paragraphs.text: We provide clear and metal braces, Invisalign<sup>®</sup> and Invisalign Teen®, Damon self-ligating braces, removable appliances for minor tooth movement, surgical orthodontics and dentofacial orthopedics, plus technologies such as iTero digital scanning and OrthoPulse to support efficient progress.

image.alt: Invisalign aligner profile image

accordion.header: How do I know which treatment is right for me or my child?

paragraphs.text: Start with a complimentary consultation. We take photos, perform a complete exam, and create a custom treatment plan so the doctor can explain options, expected timeline, costs, and any alternatives to help you choose confidently.

image.alt: Orthodontic consultation and patient discussion

accordion.header: Do you accept insurance and what payment options are available?

paragraphs.text: We review your insurance coverage and discuss in-house financing or monthly payment plans during the consultation so you understand estimated costs and available payment options before treatment begins.

image.alt: Financial consultation and payment discussion

accordion.header: How do I schedule an appointment or request a consultation?

paragraphs.text: Request visits online at https://www.taortho.com/appointment-request, or call or text Clarence at (716) 759-8323 or our Tonawanda office at (716) 875-0405. The online form collects name, email, phone, and a short comment to help us schedule the right visit.

image.alt: Request an appointment online

accordion.header: What forms should I complete before my first visit?

paragraphs.text: Complete your intake electronically at https://patient.sesamecommunications.com/mandtortho/index.html, or download printable forms: Patient Form (Child) PDF https://www.taortho.com/hub_sites/macdonald-andrew2/www/assets/uploads/files/health%20history(2).pdf and Patient Form (Adult) PDF https://www.taortho.com/hub_sites/macdonald-andrew2/www/assets/uploads/files/health%20history(3).pdf.

image.alt: Patient intake forms and online registration

accordion.header: What should I expect at the initial consultation and at the first appointment?

paragraphs.text: At the consultation we review medical and dental history, perform an oral exam, take photos or digital scans, and outline a customized treatment plan with timeline and cost options. The first appliance placement typically takes about an hour, during which the team ensures your comfort and answers questions.

image.alt: Initial orthodontic consultation and exam

accordion.header: How often are follow-up visits and what should I do if something breaks?

paragraphs.text: Follow-up visits are typically every four to eight weeks depending on your treatment. If wires, bands, or retainers become loose or break, contact the office right away, save any pieces, and bring them in. For temporary relief use orthodontic wax or a saltwater rinse until you can be seen.

image.alt: Orthodontic emergency care and temporary fixes

accordion.header: How do I care for braces and clear aligners?

paragraphs.text: For braces avoid hard or sticky foods and brush after meals using a soft-bristled brush and floss with a threader or water flosser. To relieve soreness rinse with one teaspoon of salt in eight ounces of lukewarm water and use over‑the‑counter pain relief if needed. For Invisalign<sup>®</sup> wear aligners 20 to 22 hours per day, remove them to eat and clean your teeth, and bring aligners to each visit.

image.alt: Demonstration of brushing with braces

accordion.header: What should I expect about retainers and retention?

paragraphs.text: Retention options include removable wire and acrylic retainers, Essix clear retainers, and fixed bonded retainers. Your doctor will recommend a retention plan and wear schedule based on your treatment to help protect your results long term.

image.alt: Retention options including clear and bonded retainers

accordion.header: Where can I find instructions for specific appliances like a palatal expander?

paragraphs.text: Printable instructions and step‑by‑step guides are available for appliances such as palatal expanders. See the palatal expander PDF at https://www.sesamehub.com/sesame_media/docs/palatal-expander.pdf for turning instructions and animated images.

image.alt: Palatal expander instructions and care
